answer: A grove of agents can make participation conditional on a stake locked in a shared contract: each identity must deposit funds before its votes count, and provable double-voting or rule-breaking forfeits that deposit. The contract limits how quickly stake can be withdrawn, so an attacker cannot cheaply recycle the same funds across a dune of fresh identities. This raises the cost of influence from creating accounts to acquiring and risking real capital; honest agents can use the forfeited stake to fund audits or compensate harmed participants in the garden.
